nodes.title: Henselian f-adic and affinoid rings; existence of henselizations (3.1.1-3.1.3)
nodes.statement: Lemma 3.1.1: for an f-adic ring A the following are equivalent: (i) some open subring B ⊆ A° with an open ideal I ⊆ A°° of B has (B,I) henselian; (ii) every such pair is henselian; (iii)/(iv) Spec B is henselian along its open primes for some/every open subring B of A°. Definition 3.1.2: such A is henselian; an affinoid ring is henselian if A^▷ is; complete f-adic rings are henselian and open subrings of henselian rings are henselian. Lemma 3.1.3: every f-adic ring A has a henselization ι: A -> A^h (universal among continuous maps to henselian f-adic rings) with completion ι^ an isomorphism, constructed as A_{D,I} = A ⊗_D D_I for a ring of definition D with ideal of definition I and D_I the henselization of the pair (D,I), topologised by {I^n D_I}; for affinoid rings A^h = ((A^▷)^h, (A^+)^h) with (A^+)^h integrally closed in (A^▷)^h by [EGA IV.18.12.15]. Section-wide caveat: §3.1 allows arbitrary f-adic rings, dropping the standing hypotheses (1.1.1).
hypotheses: f-adic rings, not necessarily complete; the hypotheses (1.1.1) of the rest of the book are not assumed in §3.1
Henselian pairs in the sense of Raynaud [R, XI §2 Def. 3]; the criteria (1) (Gabber [G]) and (2) (integral extensions with I'^n b ∈ B') are used in the proof of 3.1.1
proofSteps: Prove criteria (1) and (2) for henselian pairs (the proof of (2) via clopen decompositions of finite Y' -> X' after base change).
Show independence of the open subring B and open ideal I via the integral closures D, E of B, B' in A° and V(I'E) = V(A°°).
Construct A_{D,I} and prove the universal property from the universal property of D_I and uniqueness of continuous extensions (ring maps t_1, t_2 on D_I agreeing on D coincide).
Affinoid case: (A^+)^h is a ring of integral elements of (A^▷)^h and the two universal maps agree.
acceptance: A complete affinoid ring is henselian; the henselization does not change the completion.
(A^h)^+ = (A^+)^h, i.e. the plus-ring is henselized along with the ring, as the roadmap's 'track the plus ring in every completion' requires.

nodes.title: Special and pro-special subsets of Spa A and the henselization along rational subsets (3.1.4-3.1.10)
nodes.statement: Lemma 3.1.4: for a rational subset U of Spa A there is a henselian affinoid ring G_A(U) with im Spa(h) ⊆ U, universal among continuous maps to henselian affinoid rings with image in U; for U = R(T_1/s_1,...,T_n/s_n) it is the henselization of A⟨T_1/s_1,...,T_n/s_n⟩ (proved as [Hu, 1.3], using that maximal ideals of henselian f-adic rings are closed). (3.1.5): A(U) := G_A(U)^▷, the henselization of A along U, a presheaf on rational subsets. Definition 3.1.6: U ⊆ Spa A is special if U = S(D|E / t) = {x : |d(x)| ≤ |t(x)| ≠ 0 for d ∈ D, |e(x)| < |t(x)| for e ∈ E} with (D ∪ E ∪ {t})·A^▷ open; pro-special if an intersection of special subsets. Lemma 3.1.7: V is special iff V = {x ∈ U : |f_i(x)| < 1} for a rational U and f_i ∈ O_A(U). Corollary 3.1.8: special subsets are locally closed and constructible; pro-special subsets are convex and pro-constructible. Corollary 3.1.9: special subsets of Spa B for B = (O_A(U), O_A^+(U)) correspond to special subsets of Spa A inside U, and Spa A^ ≅ Spa A preserves special subsets. Lemma 3.1.10 (A Tate): locally closed constructible subsets are finite unions of special subsets open in the union; closed special subsets are the sets S(∅|E / t) with A^▷ = (E ∪ {t})A^▷ and closed constructible subsets are finite unions of them; open special subsets are rational; every special subset is the intersection of an open and a closed special subset.
hypotheses: A an affinoid ring; Lemma 3.1.10 requires A Tate
Lemma 3.1.4 and 3.1.9 import [Hu, 1.3, 1.5] and [Hu1, 3.10], [Hu4, 3.4.11] (unread)
proofSteps: Represent special subsets through rational subsets and strict inequalities (3.1.7) using density of A^▷[T/s] in O_A(U) and [Hu1, 3.10].
For Tate A: closedness criterion via the closure formula (2) L̄ = ∩_n S(D|E_n / t^n) and the convex-subgroup construction v/H.
acceptance: Every rational subset is special; a closed special subset in the Tate case has the form {|e(x)| < |t(x)| for all e ∈ E}.

nodes.title: Henselization of an affinoid ring along a pro-special subset: triples, construction, universal property and examples (3.1.11-3.1.13)
nodes.statement: (3.1.11): a triple (A,B,I) (B ⊆ A a subring, I an ideal of B) is henselian if (B,I) is a henselian pair; its henselization is (A ⊗_B B^h, B^h, I^h) for a henselization (B^h, I^h) of (B,I). Proposition/Definition 3.1.12: for a pro-special U = ∩_i S(D_i|E_i / t_i) and a pair (B,P) with B ⊆ A^+ a subring over which A^+ is integral and P ⊆ (A^▷)^{oo} an ideal of B with P·A^▷ open (e.g. (A^+, (A^▷)^{oo})), let F = A^▷[1/t_i], G = B[d/t_i, e/t_i], J = (P ∪ {e/t_i})G, and put A(U) := F^h for the henselization (F^h, G^h, J^h); then (i) A(U) is independent of the presentation and of (B,P), (ii) U ↦ A(U) is a presheaf on pro-special subsets restricting to (3.1.5) on rational subsets, (iii) continuous maps f: A -> B' with Spa(f)(V) ⊆ U induce compatible maps A(U) -> B'(V). Proof: define V(X) ⊆ Spv K for a triple X = (K,L,M) as the valuations bounded by 1 on L and < 1 on M; saturated triples (L integrally closed, M radical); (1) (X^c)^h ≅ (X^h)^c; (2) for a henselian saturated triple, L and M are recovered from V(X) and every prime of K is a support of some v ∈ V(X); then (3) the saturation Y of the henselization of (F,G,J) is universal among henselian saturated triples Z with im V(f) ⊆ r^{-1}(U), where r: Spv A^▷ -> Spv(A^▷, Q) is the retraction and (4) r^{-1}(U) is the set of primary generalizations of U. Example 3.1.13: (i) for A with the I-adic topology, A^h along I is the henselization of (A,A^+) along Spa(A,A^+); (ii) the henselization of A along a closed P ⊆ V(I) (or a point) is the henselization of (A,A) along π^{-1}(P) ⊆ Spa(A,A) (with π = the map of [Hu, 4.1] when A is noetherian); (iii) for s ∈ A and B = (A,A)(1/s), (A^h)_s is the henselization of B along λ^{-1}(P), where λ: Spa B -> V(s) agrees with λ: d(Spf A) -> Spf A when Spf A is of type (S); (iv) the henselization of an affinoid field (K,K^+) along its closed point is the henselization of K with respect to K^+ of (2.3.9).

nodes.title: The fundamental comparison theorem for pro-special subsets (3.2.1-3.2.5) and the acyclicity of relative balls (3.2.4)
nodes.statement: Theorem 3.2.1: for an affinoid ring A (not necessarily complete), a pro-special U ⊆ Spa A with henselization A(U) and Y = Spec A(U), and G a set (resp. ind-finite group, resp. abelian torsion group), there are natural isomorphisms H^n(Y, G_Y) ≅ H^n(U, G_U) for n = 0 (resp. n ∈ {0,1}, resp. n ∈ N_0), where U denotes the pseudo-adic space (Spa A, U). Corollary 3.2.2: for complete A, H^n(Spec A^▷, G) ≅ H^n(Spa A, G). Corollary 3.2.3: the same for Tate algebras of topologically finite type over k. Lemma 3.2.5 (Gabber-type affine analogue of proper base change): for A henselian along I and F an abelian torsion sheaf, H^n(Spec A, F) ≅ H^n(Spec A/I, F_0); proof delegated to [Hu3]. Example 3.2.4: for a rigid variety X over k with residue characteristic p and the closed polydisc B(r) (radii in sqrt|k^*|), F ≅ t_* t^* F and R^i t_* t^* F = 0 (i > 0) for (P − {p})-torsion F; likewise for open polydiscs via 3.9.2; proved through the pseudo-adic statement (γ) for B(s,m)_X and abelian (P − char^+(X))-torsion sheaves, in three steps: (I) constant coefficients over the spectrum of an algebraically closed affinoid field whose support contains the closed point, via 3.2.1, the henselization C of the polynomial ring along pB, the smooth base change theorem for Spec C_a -> Spec C and Lemma 3.2.5; (II) constructible sheaves by dévissage to j_!G_U; (III) general X by strict localizations and 2.6.1.
hypotheses: 3.2.1: A an affinoid ring, possibly incomplete; U pro-special; constant coefficients only
3.2.4: F a torsion sheaf with torsion prime to the residue characteristics char^+(X); radii in sqrt|k^*| (closed balls) or with ∞ (open balls)

nodes.title: Etale morphisms and the etale site of a formal scheme of type (S); identification with the reduced special scheme
nodes.statement: For formal schemes X, Y of type (S), f: Y -> X is etale if it is adic and for every open U ⊆ X and every ideal of definition I ⊆ O_U the scheme morphism Y ×_X (U, O_U/I) -> (U, O_U/I) is etale. X_et is Et/X (type-(S) formal schemes etale over X) with surjective families as coverings. With I the ideal of functions vanishing at all points, X_red = (X, O_X/I) is a reduced scheme and Z/X ↦ Z ×_X X_red/X_red is an equivalence of sites (X_red)_et ≅ X_et by [EGA IV.18.1.2]; X_et is often identified with (X_red)_et. A morphism f: X -> Y of formal schemes induces f: X_et -> Y_et by base change (Y' etale of type (S) over Y gives X ×_Y Y' etale of type (S) over X).
hypotheses: Formal schemes of type (S) (Huber §1.9 condition (S))
Topological invariance of the etale site [EGA IV.18.1.2]

nodes.title: Comparison theorem for proper morphisms of schemes after base change to an adic space (Theorem 3.7.2, Lemma 3.7.3)
nodes.statement: (3.7.1): R an adic space, S a scheme, φ: R -> S a morphism of locally ringed spaces, X, Y schemes locally of finite type over S with an S-morphism f; X^ad = X ×_S R, Y^ad = Y ×_S R ([Hu, 3.8]) and f^ad; φ_X, φ_Y induce morphisms of sites (3.2.8) with a commutative square. Theorem 3.7.2: if f is proper and Λ is a torsion ring, the base change transformation φ_Y^* R^+ f_* -> R^+ f^ad_* φ_X^* on D^+(X_et, Λ) is an isomorphism. Proof: reduce to Y = S affine, R affinoid, and (by proper base change for schemes along Spec O_R(R) -> S) to S = Spec O_R(R) with φ the identity-induced map; for a geometric point ξ of R with image η in S, the strict localization R(ξ) is Spa(B, B^+) for B the strict henselization of O_R(R) at supp η and B^+ = {v ≤ 1} for a valuation v extending ξ, topologised by {I^n B^+} (proof of 2.5.13); f^ad is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (3.7.3), so (R^n f^ad_* φ_X^*F)_ξ = H^n(X^ad ×_R Spa(B,B^+), G) by 2.6.1, while (R^n f_*F)_η = H^n(X ×_S Spec B, L); since B^+ is henselian along I and X^ad ×_R Spa(B,B^+) = (X ×_S Spec B) ×_{Spec B} Spa(B,B^+), 3.2.10 (with the pro-special subset Spa(B,B^+) and the proper map X ×_S Spec B -> Spec B) identifies the two. Lemma 3.7.3: for proper f, f^ad is separated and quasi-compact (separated since X ↦ X^ad preserves fibre products and closed embeddings; quasi-compact by Chow's lemma when O_R(R) is noetherian and non-discrete, or trivially when discrete; the remark notes f^ad is even proper, by 5.7.3.ii for analytic R and [Hu4, 3.12.8] in general).
hypotheses: f proper; Λ a torsion ring; R an adic space and φ a morphism of locally ringed spaces
Lemma 3.7.3's quasi-compactness proof as written uses noetherianity of O_R(R) in the non-discrete case (Chow's lemma); the general case is delegated to [Hu4, 3.12.8]
Imports: proper base change for schemes, 2.5.13 (structure of strict localizations), 2.6.1, 3.2.10
proofSteps: Reductions to affine S = Spec O_R(R); strict localization at ξ as Spa(B,B^+); stalk comparison via 2.6.1 and 3.2.10.

nodes.title: Comparison theorem for schemes of finite type over a complete non-archimedean field (Theorem 3.8.1) and its proof routes; the excision lemma 3.8.2
nodes.statement: Let k be a complete non-archimedean field, X, Y schemes locally of finite type over k, f: X -> Y a k-morphism of finite type, X^rig, Y^rig the associated rigid varieties, φ_X, φ_Y the morphisms of sites. Let n be a natural number, prime to char k if char k > 0. Theorem 3.8.1: for every constructible Z/nZ-module F on X_et and every q, the base change map φ_Y^* R^q f_* F -> R^q f^rig_* φ_X^* F is bijective (display lost in OCR). Proof routes given by the source: if char k = 0, as the comparison over C in [SGA 4, XVI.4], using the proper comparison 3.7.2, the cohomological purity theorem 3.9.1(b) and Lemma 3.8.2; if char k > 0, as Berkovich's comparison [Ber1, 7.5], using cohomology with proper support for (partially proper) morphisms of rigid varieties with a comparison theorem (5.7.2) and Poincaré duality (7.5.3). Lemma 3.8.2: for a commutative triangle of k-schemes U -> X -> Y with g: X -> Y proper and f: U -> X, h: U -> Y open embeddings with f(U) = g^{-1}(h(U)), and F an abelian sheaf on (U^rig)_et, the natural morphism h^rig_! F -> R g^rig_* f^rig_! F is an isomorphism; proof: pass to adic spaces, where g' is quasi-compact and separated (3.7.3); for y ∈ Y' − h'(U') the strict localization Y'(y) maps into Y' − h'(U') since that set is closed under generalizations (2.5.13.i), so the preimage of f'_! F' on X' ×_{Y'} Y'(y) vanishes and (R^n g'_* f'_! F')_y = 0 by 2.6.1.
hypotheses: k complete non-archimedean; f of finite type; F constructible Z/nZ with n prime to char k when char k > 0 (no restriction on the residue characteristic in the statement, but the char 0 route uses purity 3.9.1(b), whose hypothesis (b) requires n prime to char(S), finiteness of the set E of residue characteristics with char k(s) = 0 and invertibility of each p ∈ E, F locally constant of finite type and |S| closed under generalizations)
